result.target_topic: Recognition of Funded Status of Pension and Postretirement Plans
result.target_summary: The firm recognizes the funded status of its defined benefit pension and postretirement plans in the consolidated balance sheets, recording $73 million in other assets and $344 million in other liabilities as of December 2024, compared to $93 million in other assets and $449 million in other liabilities as of December 2023.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure D570 covers both the maintenance of unfunded postretirement benefit plans (medical/life insurance) and the recognition of their funded status in the balance sheets. In 2024, these aspects are split: D554 covers the maintenance of the unfunded postretirement plans, and D555 covers the recognition of funded status with specific asset/liability figures. Both 2024 disclosures are counterparts to the single 2023 disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Underfunded defined benefit pension plans data
comparisons.peer_summary: The text presents the aggregate projected benefit obligation (PBO), accumulated benefit obligation (ABO), and fair value of plan assets for defined benefit pension plans where PBO or ABO exceeds assets, noting that as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, only nonqualified plans met this underfunded criteria.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the funded status of defined benefit pension plans by presenting data for plans where obligations exceed assets. Citigroup (C) explicitly states that for its 2024 and 2023 fiscal years, only nonqualified plans met the criteria of PBO/ABO exceeding plan assets (c_2024_8_P293_S002), whereas Goldman Sachs (GS) reports specific aggregate dollar amounts for these funded status positions on its balance sheet, showing a decrease in both other assets and other liabilities related to these plans from 2023 to 2024 (gs_2024_8_P717_S002, gs_2024_8_P717_S003).

sentences.text: The firm recognizes the funded status of its defined benefit pension and postretirement plans, measured as the difference between the fair value of the plan assets and the benefit obligation, in the consolidated balance sheets.
As of December 2024, other assets included $73 million (related to overfunded pension plans) and other liabilities included $344 million related to these plans.
As of December 2023, other assets included $93 million (related to overfunded pension plans) and other liabilities included $449 million related to these plans.

At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the aggregate projected benefit obligation (PBO), the aggregate accumulated benefit obligation (ABO) and the aggregate fair value of plan assets are presented for all defined benefit pension plans with a PBO in excess of plan assets and for all defined benefit pension plans with an ABO in excess of plan assets as follows:
(1)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, only the nonqualified plans' PBO and ABO exceeded plan assets.
